traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 024.0-DEV-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE-REFS are satisfied.
- Core Functionality (ignore backtick-wrapped keywords): normalizeCommentLine uses a centralized regex `/`[^`]*`/g` to replace any backtick-wrapped span with spaces of equal length before looking for @story/@req/@supports. Tests explicitly verify backtick-wrapped `@story` and `@req` produce output with no annotation tags. - Common Patterns: The tests cover documentation-like patterns such as "This rule uses `@story` and other tags" and "`@story` + `@req` docs", ensuring these do not surface as annotations after normalization. - Real Annotations Detected: A mixed case is tested where the line contains both `@supports` (in backticks) and a real @story annotation plus path; normalizeCommentLine returns only the real @story... line, proving real annotations outside backticks are still detected. - Multi-Line Support: normalizeCommentLine operates on individual lines and is used by the shared validation helpers. The behavior is line-agnostic; combined with existing multi-line handling in the annotation validation logic, this satisfies the requirement that any line containing backtick-wrapped content is filtered correctly. - No Regression: A full Jest run (npm test -- --runInBand --verbose) passes all suites, including those unrelated to this story, indicating no regressions from the change. - Documentation: The JSDoc on normalizeCommentLine explicitly documents the backtick filtering behavior and its purpose (preserving character boundaries while stripping inline code spans).
The implementation is centralized in normalizeCommentLine, carries correct traceability annotations (@supports with this story and requirements), has targeted tests that map directly to REQ-IGNORE-INLINE-CODE, REQ-PRESERVE-BOUNDARIES, and REQ-CENTRALIZED-FILTER, and all tests pass. Therefore the story is fully implemented.
